The 'dips' are just the low phases of continuous variability, not discrete occultations. explanation: Most likely a crowding/window artefact from a close resolved neighbour: ipd_frac_multi_peak = 1.0 (every transit shows a double image), BP has blended transits and a slightly high BP/RP excess. At t~775 G drops 2.8% in both fields of view, but BP and RP drop only ~0.8-1.0%. A real occultation of the star cannot make G fall deeper than both BP and RP, because G spans those bands. The t=151.8 dip is a single flagged fov-2 epoch where G is again deeper than RP. That points to G-window or image-parameter flux loss at particular scan angles. Apart from the dips, the star varies coherently by ~0.5% in all bands, probably spots or rotation.
